slides.teacher_cue: A morphological word family is a group of words that all share the same root but differ in their affixes (prefixes and suffixes). act → action → active → activity → actor → react → interaction → overreact. form → inform → reform → transform → formation → formal → uniform → performance. nation → national → nationality → international → nationalism → nationalise. Knowing one word in a family gives you access to all the others — the meaning stays connected.
slides.expected_response: Students generate word families from a root and explain how affixes change the part of speech and meaning.
slides.correction_move: Model: start with act. Add -ion → action (noun). Add -ive → active (adjective). Add -ity → activity (noun). Add re- → react (verb). Add inter- → interaction (noun). Students build family trees.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students treating derived words as completely new vocabulary rather than extensions of known words.

slides.teacher_cue: Say national — nation + al. From nation (a country). Reveal and blend.

slides.correction_move: Model national orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for -tion in nation and -al suffix creating an adjective.
